population.note: 11% of US adults currently on a GLP-1 for weight loss, 15% ever (Gallup, May–Jun 2026; up from 3%/6% in 2024). KFF (Oct–Nov 2025) counting all reasons: 12% current, 18% ever. Use peaks at ages 50–64 (~22%) and roughly halves after 65 (~9%). Pediatric: approved 12+; prescribing to children 8–11 with obesity rose from 0.03% (2019) to 9.3% (2026) of those with a prescription event — still ~0.6% of children with obesity overall; upper-income children 55% more likely to be prescribed. Persistence: roughly a third of weight-management starters remain on therapy at one year (34–36%); 36–47% of those who stop restart within a year. US adult obesity fell from 39.9% (2022) to 36.4% (2026). Income split and cycled-off share not published as clean national figures — leave null at step 0; simulated steps may estimate them and must flag fictional:true. [S1, S2, S3, S4, S5, S6, S7]

access.public_coverage: Medicare: 18-month GLP-1 Bridge pilot (Jul 2026–Dec 2027) covering obesity for beneficiaries meeting BMI/comorbidity criteria; Medicare pays ~$245/month, beneficiary copay ~$50; ~10% of enrollees newly eligible. Medicaid expected to follow at the same rates. CBO: ≥$35B added federal spend 2026–2034. Cash-pay via TrumpRx and manufacturer direct channels ~$350/month trending to ~$245; oral initial doses priced at $149–150.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India (patent lapsed Mar 2026): 40+ generic brands at roughly $8–48/month; Novo cut Indian brand prices ~35% within two weeks. Canada: first G7 generic approvals Apr–May 2026 (Dr. Reddy's, Apotex, Sandoz), ~CAD 88–120/month. Brazil approvals granted. Cost-plus studies put generic injectable semaglutide at $28–140 per person-year, oral at $186–380, available in ~160 countries by end-2026. US semaglutide exclusivity runs to roughly 2031–32; no FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide (generic liraglutide approved 2024–25).
access.note: List prices: Wegovy $1,349, Ozempic ~$998; almost nobody pays list. Employer coverage for weight management fell from 72% (2025) to 60% (2026) per Business Group on Health (WTW: 57%→53%); 14% have dropped or plan to drop by 2027; Starbucks dropped weight-loss coverage Oct 2026; GLP-1s were 11.4% of claims among covering employers (2025). Compounding/telehealth gray market shrinking under FDA pressure: 30 warning letters (Mar 2026) + 25 (Jun 2026); FDA proposed excluding semaglutide/tirzepatide/liraglutide from the 503B bulks list (Apr 30, 2026); >1,700 adverse-event reports tied to compounded product by May 2026; Novo sued Hims & Hers (Feb 2026). Route: weekly injectables still dominant by volume, but oral Wegovy (approved Dec 22, 2025; ~170k prescriptions in first three weeks) and Foundayo/orforglipron (approved Apr 1, 2026) are shifting the mix. [S8–S19]

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill, 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: alcohol reduction — RCT evidence, no approval: Lancet May 2026 (n=108, AUD + obesity) semaglutide cut heavy-drinking days ~41 pp vs ~26 pp placebo; oral semaglutide phase 2 in AUD positive (Jul 2026); ~3% of US adults have obesity plus heavy drinking
microdosing / 'metabolic health' use by people without obesity, via telehealth
pediatric under-12 use off-label under specialist care
reward/craving reduction for nicotine and other compulsions — anecdotal and observational
drugs.pipeline_note: CagriSema (semaglutide + amylin analogue, ~20%) NDA filed Dec 2025, FDA decision window late 2026, but failed non-inferiority vs tirzepatide in REDEFINE-4 (Feb 2026). Retatrutide (triple GIP/GLP-1/glucagon) phase 3: 28.3% mean loss at 80 weeks, up to 30.3% at 104 weeks in BMI≥35; 11.3% discontinuation for adverse events; dysesthesia signal; BLA planned ~Q1 2027, approval 2027–28. Amycretin (single-molecule GLP-1/amylin) entered phase 3 May 2026 (~22% in phase 2). Survodutide phase 3 (~16.6%). MariTide monthly injectable in development. Muscle-preserving adjuncts (bimagrumab) and amylin monotherapies in trials. Global incretin market ~$76B (2025), forecasts $150–162B by 2030–31. [S20–S24]

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Most common class effect; concentrated at initiation and dose escalation; leading cause of discontinuation.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; Ozempic label updated Jan 2025 'not recommended in severe gastroparesis'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Listed adverse effect; long-term RCTs have not confirmed a causal link; absolute risk low.

Commonly cited that ~25–30% of weight lost is lean mass; concern concentrated in older adults and long-term users; bone-density and musculoskeletal (osteoporosis, gout, osteomalacia) signal in a 2026 AAOS abstract.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; industry response is muscle-preserving combination drugs in trials.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Cohort studies conflict (one five-year cohort ~2× risk; others null).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: EMA PRAC (Jun 2025) labelled as 'very rare' for semaglutide; no US class label.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: EMA, MHRA and a 2025 systematic review found no causal association.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA requested removal of the suicidal-ideation warning from Saxenda, Wegovy and Zepbound labels (Jan 13, 2026).

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Patient-reported, widely covered in 2026 press; mechanistically plausible via GLP-1 receptors in dopaminergic reward circuits; not quantified; trials were not designed to detect it. Same mechanism underlies the alcohol-use-disorder results.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None. Manufacturer: 'no data to share on anhedonia'.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Trial data: ~two-thirds of lost weight regained within a year (STEP-1 extension); some 2026 real-world claims data show much smaller regain — the figures conflict.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None; drives chronic-therapy framing by manufacturers and payers.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Narrative review (Feb 2026, pooled n≈480k) flags deficiencies with reduced intake.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No data. Roughly four years of rigorous RCT follow-up exists.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements attached to new approvals (e.g. Foundayo).

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: >1,700 FDA adverse-event reports tied to compounded semaglutide/tirzepatide by May 2026.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning-letter waves (Sep 2025, Mar 2026, Jun 2026); proposed exclusion from 503B bulks list.

food_and_beverage.state: Measurable volume pressure in snacks, confectionery and sugary drinks; GLP-1 households ~21–23% of US households and projected to be 35% of F&B units by 2030; JPMorgan estimates $30–55B of annual F&B revenue eliminated by 2030; protein is the dominant marketing callout; 'GLP-1-friendly' SKUs and portion formats proliferating. ING: near-term calorie-demand impact in Europe only ~0.25%.

alcohol.state: Diageo and Brown-Forman name GLP-1 adoption a top-three structural threat; the top 10% of drinkers are ~60% of sales and a third of heavy drinkers in survey data shift down a category on-drug; no offsetting growth category exists.

restaurants.state: Traffic holding — GLP-1 users remain frequent restaurant customers but order differently (smaller plates, premium, indulgent cocktails as 'occasion'); premiumisation offsets volume.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists hit (Torrid −14.3% YoY; DXL attributing part of a 6% decline to ~25% of its customers on-drug and deferring purchases); mainstream apparel sees a second wave of re-buying at smaller sizes.

fitness.state: Repositioning around muscle preservation and 'GLP-1 companion' programmes; strength training and protein marketed to on-drug consumers.

insurance.state: Employer coverage for weight management retreating (72%→60%); pharmacy trend +11.5% in 2026; GLP-1s ~11% of claims where covered; Medicare/Medicaid absorbing cost via negotiated $245; prior authorisation and BMI thresholds tightening.

pharma.state: Duopoly (Novo Nordisk, Eli Lilly) with Lilly ahead on efficacy and the oral; price erosion beginning via government deals and ex-US generics; next-generation (retatrutide, CagriSema, amycretin) and a 770-molecule GLP-1R competitive field; market ~$76B 2025 → $150B+ by 2030.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A thin body is increasingly read as 'on it'; 37% of adults know someone taking a GLP-1; being on the drug is semi-public and increasingly unremarkable in affluent and middle-aged circles.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Access skews to the insured and the cash-rich; children of upper-income households are 55% more likely to be prescribed; ex-US generics are making thinness cheap abroad while the US still rations by coverage.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Smaller portions and fewer snacks are normal in GLP-1 households; 'food noise' has entered everyday language; restaurants and CPG are re-engineering around less appetite, not less spending.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Anecdotal reports of libido and relationship changes on-drug; 'Ozempic personality' coverage includes people describing falling out of love. Not quantified.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite is being reframed from a trait to a treatable signal; craving of all kinds (food, alcohol, nicotine) is on the table as pharmacological territory.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: Unquantified. Reported with enough consistency (Washington Post, Boston Globe, AP, 2026) to be named; clinicians call it uncommon; dose reduction reportedly restores motivation in some.
interior_life.framing: Side effect and curiosity. The same mechanism is simultaneously being pursued as treatment (alcohol use disorder RCTs) — the feature/bug ambiguity is already present.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Not studied. Anecdotes of lost drive; also anecdotes of improved focus from quieted craving.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: Not studied. Users report muted enjoyment of music, socialising, exercise; some gravitate to high-intensity flavours (sour candy) to feel reward.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Anecdotal: reduced desire and emotional connection in some users.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access and pro-speed: Foundayo approved in 50 days under the FDA Commissioner's National Priority Voucher; Medicare obesity coverage launched via demonstration programmes; simultaneously an aggressive crackdown on compounders and telehealth marketing.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Price-controlled public access via Medicare pilot ($245 to Medicare / $50 copay) and TrumpRx cash channel (~$350→$245; orals $149–150). Medicaid at the same rates expected.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Coverage conditioned on BMI/comorbidity criteria and prior authorisation; employers tightening eligibility; no adherence monitoring or benefit conditioning beyond standard prior auth.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: US holds brand exclusivity to ~2031–32 while India, Canada and Brazil have generics in 2026; the price gap (US ~$350–1,349 vs India ~$8–48) is a visible political fact; manufacturers trading price cuts for tariff relief and Medicare access.

events.event: Trump administration deals with Lilly and Novo: Medicare to cover obesity drugs at $245 with $50 copay; TrumpRx cash channel; oral launches capped at $149–150
FDA approves oral Wegovy (semaglutide 25 mg), the first oral GLP-1 for obesity
Semaglutide patent lapses in India; 40+ generic brands launch at up to 80% below brand; FDA issues 30 warning letters to GLP-1 telehealth marketers
FDA approves Foundayo (orforglipron), first small-molecule oral GLP-1, in 50 days; Canada approves first G7 generic semaglutide; FDA proposes excluding semaglutide/tirzepatide from 503B compounding
Lancet RCT: semaglutide cuts heavy-drinking days in alcohol use disorder; retatrutide phase 3 reports 28.3% weight loss; 'Ozempic personality' enters mainstream coverage
Gallup: 11% of US adults on a GLP-1 for weight loss (3% in 2024); Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot begins; employer coverage for weight loss falls to 60%

open_tensions: Price is collapsing abroad and being negotiated down at home while employers retreat — who pays, and for whom, is unresolved.
The same reward mechanism is a complaint (anhedonia) and a therapy (alcohol use disorder) at once; no one has decided which it is.
Two-thirds of starters stop within a year and most restart — the population is cycling, and nobody knows what cycling does over a decade.
Prescribing to children is rare but rising 300-fold, skewed to the affluent, with no long-horizon data.
